To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energetic cost of walking and running with armour is much higher than unloaded locomotion, and that the increased energetic cost of locomotor activity in Medieval soldiers' armour is explained by the additional weight, the extra force that is required to move the limbs and impaired ventilation.
wearing steel plate armour increases the energy cost of walking and running by 1.9–2.3 fold.
wearing Medieval armour increased the energetic cost of walking and running.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of wearing armour on Medieval soldier's physical performance.
the effects of wearing armour on the energetics and locomotor performance in Medieval soldiers.
the effects of wearing armour on locomotor energetical and biomechanical performance in Medieval soldiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the energy cost of locomotion is much more ener-getically expensive during armoured walking or running, when compared with unloaded locomotion at similar speed.
Medieval armour was not a good choice for a long-distance march or a prolonged military campaign.
the armour was a major limiting factor in Medieval soldiers' performance and it is likely to have contributed to their defeat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wearing armour was detrimental for locomotion, and that Medieval soldiers' physical capacity declined with age.

the extra energy cost of locomotion and physical performance in armour is mostly due to the additional mass, but the impaired breathing and increased limb movement also contribute to the increased energy cost of locomotor activities in armour.

wearing a typical suit of armour during locomotion increases the energetic cost of walking and running by approximately 2.1 and 1.8 times, respectively, and reduces the maximal speed by 30% for both modes of locomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Medieval soldiers were not as agile as they were perceived to be.
the cost of locomotion increases with increasing mass, and this cost is even higher when the mass is concentrated in the upper body.
wearing heavy armour has a profound impact on soldiers' performance and that this is likely to have had an effect on military strategy and tactics.
